requirement: A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
rationale:
The span rules are implemented and tested, but the implementation also accepts indented fences, which no requirement specifies and no test covers.

**What is implemented and tested**
- `definition_blocks` and `colon_fence` in `src/lib.rs` are marked `{impl}`.
  - They require an opening fence of at least three colons followed immediately by `{req}`, then whitespace and a valid name. `::: {req}`-style or no-space variants are not matched.
  - The closer must be a colon-only line with at least as many colons as the opener, and it must sit outside a code block. Text after the closer is therefore excluded.
  - The body is the raw text between the fence lines, taken as `body_start..body_end`. It keeps headings, examples and blank lines, including `:::` and headings inside code fences.
  - Colon lines shorter than the opener stay in the body.
- `collect_definitions` in `src/evidence.rs` takes `content[body_start..body_end].trim()`. That is the "leading and trailing whitespace excluded" rule, and it carries a `{impl}` marker.
- Tests carry `{test}` markers for these cases:
  - `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text` covers a body with a code-fenced `:::`, ATX and setext headings, and text after the closer.
  - `a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive` covers a longer opener with a nested shorter directive.
  - `reports_a_missing_closing_colon_fence` covers the unclosed case.
  - `validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines` is also marked `{test}`.

**Gap**
- `colon_fence` accepts up to three leading spaces before the opening fence and before the closing fence (`line.trim_start_matches(' ')`, rejected only above 3).
  - The span requirement says nothing about indentation. `requirements.ci.fence_lengths`, `identifiers` and `definition_errors` don't either, and a search for "indent" found no requirement text that does.
  - So this is behavior in the `{impl}` code that no requirement specifies. A `   :::{req} x` line defines a requirement.
  - No test exercises or documents that behavior.
- The closer also tolerates trailing whitespace (`suffix.trim().is_empty()`). This is likewise unspecified, though it is minor.

There are no `FIXME` comments acknowledging the indentation gap, so the result is false rather than FIXME. Either the requirement should state the indentation allowance and have a test, or the implementation should drop it.

A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.

A `{req}` opening fence MAY contain four or more colons. Habeas MUST accept opening fences of any length of at least three colons. A colon-only line with fewer colons than the opener MUST remain inside the requirement body, allowing a nested colon directive. A closing fence outside a fenced code example with at least as many colons as the opener MUST end the body.

Validation MUST read the mdBook source directory from `[book].src` in `book.toml`, using `src` when the setting is absent. It MUST report an unreadable or malformed book configuration and reject an empty, absolute, or parent-traversing source path.

Requirement and reference names MUST have nonempty dot-separated segments containing only ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. An invalid `{req}` directive or role MUST remain literal and MUST NOT define or reference a requirement. For nested chapter paths, a leading `reqs/` and a final `index` or `README` segment MUST be omitted from the requirement namespace.
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under

Habeas MUST identify a Rust item by the pair of its `rust_file`, following the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`, and a `rust_item` selector derived from a `syn` parse of that file. The selector MUST describe syntactic ancestry within the file and MUST NOT resolve Rust modules across files or use line numbers as identity. Named items MUST use kind-and-name segments such as `fn[run]` and `struct[Packet]`. Impl segments MUST distinguish inherent from trait impls using their syntactic self type and optional trait path. Otherwise identical selectors MUST have deterministic source-order disambiguators. A `use` declaration MUST have a positional selector `use#N`, where N is its one-based position among sibling `use` declarations; its import target MUST NOT form part of the selector. Other items without a suitable name MUST have a kind and positional disambiguator. Selector spelling MUST be documented and reversible when names or types contain delimiter characters.

In Markdown, escaped roles and role-looking text in inline code, fenced code, or raw HTML MUST remain literal and MUST NOT count as references. A `{req}` directive inside a fenced code example and a legacy inline `{req}` role MUST NOT define a requirement.

The book preprocessor MUST escape requirement names and link targets when inserting badge HTML. It MUST encode badge label and message text in Shields.io URL path components so punctuation cannot change the badge URL structure.
